items.q: The old guard especially Dmitri Tiomkin and those people did not like something like this come along.

ctx.x: And you got an Academy Award nomination or didn’t?
Sure didn't, got frozen right out, Hollywood did not take very kindly to jazz in those days. The old guard especially Dmitri Tiomkin and those people did not like something like this come along.

items.title: Mandel Johnny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: No, that started a long time ago in 1952 with the title song when Dimitri Tiomkin wrote, “High Noon.”

ctx.x: Do you think that the success that Mancini had with some of the songs that came from his movies had something to do with that? Things like, “Moon River, “ and, “Charade,” and what have you?

No, that started a long time ago in 1952 with the title song when Dimitri Tiomkin wrote, “High Noon.” The title song was really with us all through the 50s and it wasn’t necessarily a good thing but it was a good thing for song writers.
I guess even earlier with, “Laura,” for example.
